answer: A sponsor carries 46% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the vertex liability is published in the cedar ledger at admission, the beacon audit shows the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must hence place its own capital behind every alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 32 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
